$comment: The committed expected-difference list for the three ARXML goldens.
Written BEFORE the writer was changed and before a single golden was regenerated, by hand,
from the design: an unmatched difference must fail a test rather than reach a reviewer's
attention. `packages/tools/tests/test_arxml_golden_differences.py` computes the observed difference
between `differences/before/<name>.arxml` (the exact pre-change bytes, committed for this) and
the golden beside it, and asserts it EQUALS the entry below.
How a difference is measured. Each document is flattened into one STRUCTURAL LINE per XML
element, `{tag}|{path}|{DEST}|{text}`, where `path` is the SHORT-NAME chain of the element
itself or of its nearest named ancestor, `DEST` is the reference attribute or empty, and
`text` is the element's own leaf text or empty. Three axes are then compared:
* `renamed` -- string substitutions applied to every line of the BEFORE document first, so
a pure rename is declared once instead of appearing as N removals and N additions;
* `structure_removed` / `structure_added` -- the multiset difference of the lines that
remain, sorted;
* `order_changes` -- for every named parent whose set of named children is unchanged, the
child order before and after. A reorder under a parent whose child set ALSO changed is
carried by the two multisets and is deliberately not reported twice.
What this comparison does NOT reach: attributes other than `DEST`, and whitespace. Byte
equality against the golden is `test_arxml_golden.py`'s own assertion and stays the
authority; this file is about the CHANGE between two goldens, not about either one.

reason: The writer no longer invents `SwCraftComposition`. `examples/basic/model/compositions/
Root.yaml` declares the root, so the one composition element is renamed to `Root` and
every path built from the old name follows it -- the element itself, its two
SW-COMPONENT-PROTOTYPEs, its ASSEMBLY-SW-CONNECTOR and the connector's two
CONTEXT-COMPONENT-REFs.
The prototypes also change order. They used to be the `swc` layer's read order
(ExampleConsumerSWC before ExampleSWC, because a layer is read by sorted path); they are
the root's declared `members` order now, which is ExampleSWC first.
Nothing else moves: no element is added or removed, no TARGET-*-PORT-REF changes (it has
always pointed at the TYPE's port, never at the prototype), and no TYPE-TREF changes.
The same two differences as `basic-4.2.2`, for the same two reasons, on a model root whose
root composition declares SensorSwc before ActuatorSwc while the `swc` layer reads
ActuatorSwc first. This golden carries every tag SWCraft emits, and none of the other 93
is touched: the composition change reaches nothing outside the composition element.
No difference at all, and the entry exists to say so rather than to leave the third golden
unmentioned (the committed golden set is three files, and
`GOLDEN_MODEL_ROOTS` names only two because this one is generated from a freshly created
empty tree git cannot represent).
Before the change an empty model emitted no composition because it declared no CONNECTOR;
after it, it emits none because it declares no COMPOSITION. The gate moved from the
connector layer to the compositions layer and the degenerate output is unchanged -- which
is the assertion, not a coincidence: this is the one golden whose bytes are compared
directly.
